📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ultras of Lazio’s Curva Nord have unveiled that they will temporarily lift their Stadio Olimpico boycott for their Serie A clash at home against Atalanta on December 6, but not all supporters agree with the decision.

It has been revealed that lazio supporters have been boycotting their home matches since the beginning of the calendar year in protest of owner Claudio Lotito. Fans are demanding that Lotito sell the club and had promised that they would not return to the stadium, aside from derby fixtures, until he had done so.

Despite home season tickets plummeting to around 3,000 season and away supporters regularly outnumbering home fans in the Stadio Olimpico in 2026-27, Lazio have surged to the top of the Serie A table and remain unbeaten after the first 12 league matches of the season.

Now, the Curva Nord has declared that they intend to return to the Stadio Olimpico as a one-off for Lazio’s home match against Atalanta on December 6. They are also set to be in the stands for their home match against rivals Roma the following weekend, on December 13, as the boycott did not originally apply to derby matches.

Lazio fans are also expected to attend the Supercoppa Italiana final between Inter and Lazio in San Siro on December 22.

“For the month of December, we have decided to treat ourselves to a full month of Lazio,” read a statement from the Curva Nord on Tuesday.

“A year ago, this would have been the norm for the Biancocelesti supporters, but unfortunately, a tyrannical President and his host of Giallorossi fans have forced us into this act of love, which has taken us away from our home.”.

The statement continued: “The leadership of this club has done absolutely nothing to bring the fans closer again, continuing to go in the complete opposite direction and the people of Lazio have continued to choose which side to take.

“A few exceptions have stood out, and among them there is definitely the coach, Gattuso, who has repeatedly reiterated that he understands and respects our decision, but expresses his ‘dream’ of seeing the Olimpico full of his people.

“At every away game he and the team have come and stood under the away section to receive the well-deserved applause, and we know that they are with us.

“For him, for the team, but most importantly for the youngsters and fans who have joined the protest but couldn’t get tickets for the derby, and for all the Lazio fans who suffer while being away from Lazio, we’ve decided to enter the stadium for the Lazio-Atalanta match on December 6.

“This way, we will also fire up the lads ahead of the city derby, giving them a taste of the atmosphere they will find on  December 13, showing them that we are always by their side, because they deserve it.”.

Not all Lazio supporters agree with this decision, though.

A number of comments have been left in response to the statement, which was posted on Instagram. One fan wrote: “He [Lotito] has won, as usual. As far as I’m concerned, I will only be back when I hear an apology, or when the significant news is announced.”.

Another added: “I’m sorry, but this time I don’t agree and I won’t come. Only for the derby as was agreed.”.

Sources indicate that another agreed: “I’ll stay consistent, I won’t go.” Another fan commented: “History has been saying the same thing for 20 years. Intermittent protests depending on results. Once again, he has won.”.

#174482. Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1097 w)

Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.
  • The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.
  • The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest share sale on record.

The Claude maker offered 980 million shares for sale at $83 (€76), yet began trading 34% higher at $111.50.

The opening price valued the five-year-old firm at around $2 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

Yet, after the first two days of trading, Anthropic stock closed Friday more than 20% below its opening price at $87.80, suggesting the hype had run ahead of what investors were willing to pay.

Anthropic's public listing is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

2026 was meant to be the year Wall Street’s trillion-dollar bet on what US President Donald Trump calls superintelligence (SI) started paying off.

Industry observers note that in the first half of the year, it did. Many AI stocks hit record highs as US hyperscalers like Google's Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft recorded bumper earnings.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The second half of 2026, however, has brought a lot more uncertainty.

While the stock of chipmaker Nvidia pushed even higher last month, many hyperscalers and chip or memory firms have seen erratic movements in their stock prices.

Then, after the Democrats won control of the United States Congress in the midterm elections earlier this month, technology stocks sold off again dramatically.

The Magnificent Seven — including Meta, Apple, Amazon and Tesla — lost more than $1 trillion in value in a single trading day.

In a further twist, the AI sector took another hit last week as Nvidia shares plunged nearly 10% over two days.

The sell-off followed revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman reportedly suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy.

Huang resigned from the chipmaker, sending Nvidia's shares lower still and prompting a campaign by current and former staffers, investors and other key figures in Silicon Valley to have him reinstated.

"Is this the best timing?" asked Dennis Dick, chief market strategist at the Canada-based Stock Trader Network, in an interview with DW last week.

Dick remarked Anthropic's valuation depends on whether it can deliver on a forecast by Goldman Sachs of more than $600 billion in revenue by 2030.

"If you get to a organization with $600 billion in revenue, [a] $1.3 trillion [valuation] doesn’t sound that bad," he told DW. "But when you’re talking about a company with at the moment $52 billion in revenue, it sounds like it’s overvalued.".

Other analysts, like Vivek Seth, chief executive officer of Shaires Holdings, are more bullish about the Claude maker's prospects.

"Anthropic is a once-in-a-generation organization," Seth told Bloomberg last week, noting how it has grown rapidly and has strong institutional backing. "Its IPO will establish a market-clearing valuation as conditions stabilize.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Wall Street is growing increasingly cautious about the sheer size of the AI outlay, amid warnings that future earnings may not justify the huge spending.

In September, investment bank Goldman Sachs estimated that hyperscalers need around $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their spending, leaving a gap of roughly $230 billion.

"We're not in Kansas anymore," Dick quipped, borrowing a line from the classic movie "The Wizard of Oz," which means times have changed. Now, he stated, investors are telling companies: "Show me the money.".

Other analysts, however, think it's too soon to expect the AI bubble to burst, including Kit Rees, investment strategist at London-based wealth manager Quilter, who thinks the post-election rout was a "healthy correction.".

"We’re still in the very early innings of the AI build-out," Rees told DW. "There’s still a lot of excitement around this technology and investors will want to have a slice of the pie.".

In addition to the roughly $800 billion invested in capital expenditures this year, AI hyperscalers plan to spend a further $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

Industry observers note that with many investors already running for the hills, Rees isn’t convinced the AI bubble will burst in the way skeptics expect. She thinks they should watch for stronger signs that the AI trade is maturing.

This could be "a slowdown in AI-related revenues for companies, or signs of less demand or less appetite for financing companies’ AI intends, be it through debt or through equity offerings," Rees told DW.

In a recent development, there are early signs that investors have less appetite for AI-related debt. Borrowing costs for AI infrastructure firms like CoreWeave and Oracle have soared recently. Even the cost of insuring Nvidia’s debt against default has risen 76% in a month, CNBC reported recently.

Sources indicate that "They [Oracle] have been spending, some people say, like drunken sailors," Dick told DW. "They’ve compromised their balance sheet to a point where the stock’s fallen 65% from the highs.".

In a recent development, that has not stopped Oracle, along with Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet, from continuing to problem fresh AI bonds. Since the end of last month, the four AI giants have unveiled deals worth $67 billion.

Rees noted another sign could be any new regulations that make it harder to build out US data centers, due to pressure on local water and electricity supplies.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In his upcoming book "AI Mania: Blather, Bluster, and the Bubble of All Bubbles," economist Gary Smith compares the AI boom with earlier frenzies around railways, automobiles, television and the internet. He warns of a "frightful crash" when the AI bubble eventually pops.

Recent findings suggest that when the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, the tech-heavy Nasdaq stock market index lost nearly 80% of its value. Yet, previous bubbles have often lasted far longer than expected, making the timing of any crash hard to predict.

Joachim Klement, head of market strategy at UK-based investment bank Panmure Liberum, believes a reckoning could happen as early as next year.

"My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years,” Klement told Bloomberg last month.

Editor's note: This article was first published on November 13, 2026 and was updated on November 18, 19 and 20 to reflect the latest developments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United chiefs have agreed that they must back newly introduced manager Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window, according to the Times, even though they don't normally like doing business in the winter market.

Man United prefer to do their business in the summer, like in the previous two when they have rebuilt their midfield and attack, but the club has accepted they must sign players in the New Year to help their Argentine head coach revolutionise the club following a dreadful start to the season.

Pochettino saw first-hand the huge task facing him when the Red Devils found themselves 2-0 down, and a man down, after 13 minutes of his first match in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

United ended up losing 4-0 and, as well as lying 19th in the Premier League table as we approach December, the team has also conceded more goals than any other team in the top five European leagues, in all competitions.

Their defence in particular is a major concern if they are to avoid genuinely being involved in a relegation battle this term, while their lack of a recgonised striker in the absence of the injured Benjamin Sesko has hurt them too.

Even though Michael Carrick took charge towards the beginning of January this year and United wanted to push up the standings, they didn't sign a player in that month.

Things will be different this January, and they could look to add a new left-back despite Pochettino being a big fan of Luke Shaw, having worked with him at Southampton previously.

The problem with Shaw is, that even though he's capable of being a great left-back on his day and played all 38 Premier League matches last season, he has had big injury complications at Old Trafford and is right now on a run of eight games missed.

According to the Times, United looked at signing Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde in the summer, and now the 23-year-old wants to leave the Camp Nou in January after failing to start any games for them this season.

The report adds that United could land him for £25m in the New Year, ensuring he is a lower-cost option than someone like Newcastle United's Lewis Hall.

United hold an interest in Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson, who Pochettino knows well from the USA setup, according to GIVEMESPORT sources.

The 29-year-old does have extensive Premier League experience, but there is something very tempting about signing Balde, especially for the reported £25m fee.

The Spain international has played seven times for the world champions, and he has racked up 173 appearances for Barcelona, the current LaLiga champions, although he has struggled for game time during the 2026-27 campaign.

Last term was his third league title won while playing for Barca, while he has also won four more trophies since coming through the ranks, which is impressive at the age of 23.

Balde has also played more than 30 times in the Champions League, so he brings experience from a competition the Red Devils are looking to progress in over the coming months.

The Barcelona-born full-back has all the attributes to be the perfect defender in a Pochettino system, as his strengths lie in getting forward to support the attack, his dribbling and his pace.

According to the Athletic, the 23-year-old has the physical qualities to perform at an 'elite' level, although he has frustrated some at Barcelona, including manager Hansi Flick, with the quality of his end product in the final third.

With 18 months left on his deal, January feels like a big opportunity for all parties, and while United could also move to sign a £75m star for Pochettino, they must decide if Balde is their number one left-back target.

Steven Gerrard is expecting Andoni Iraola to make several changes to the Liverpool starting XI for their Champions League fixture against Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds go into the match in Belgium off the back of their best result of the Basque’s reign so far, the 4-0 drubbing of Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday, and the European clash comes four days before the Merseyside derby away to Everton.

LFC are likely to have a near fully-fit squad for tomorrow night, and given the tight turnaround between fixtures, their former captain thinks the head coach will shuffle the pack for the game against Brugge.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Gerrard said: “I think he’ll make three or four changes, not because of the back of the performance because everyone played really well, but I think he’ll manage the squad in terms of trying to get the team in the freshest possible place, knowing how difficult the Everton game will be at the weekend.

“I think Liverpool are in a position where they can make three or four changes to the XI for Brugge – with all due respect – and win that game, and have a few people pulled back for the Merseyside derby.”.

In a recent development, want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

In selecting his starting XI for Wednesday, Iraola must be mindful that Club Brugge are ninth in the league phase standings in the Champions League, level with Liverpool on points and goal difference, so the Belgian outfit should command the utmost respect.

However, as Gerrard indicates, the Reds boss could plausibly make a few changes to his line-up without greatly weakening the team, whilst also enabling him to keep some bodies fresh for the Merseyside derby.

There may well be one or two alterations at the back – Kostas Tsimikas has tended to come in for Milos Kerkez for European games, and there might also be a start for one of Joe Gomez or the fit-again Jeremie Frimpong.

Trey Nyoni could come back into the midfield at the expense of either Dominik Szoboszlai or Alexis Mac Allister, although the latter would be very difficult to omit on current form.

In attack, Victor Munoz’s goal off the bench on Sunday might be enough to propel him into the starting XI, and Bradley Barcola – who was unhappy with his own performance against Man United – could potentially be held in reserve among the substitutes for a recharge.

That Iraola has the scope to make those few proposed changes and still field a team capable of winning in Belgium (and in the derby on Sunday) shows how much strength in depth Liverpool can boast when they have relatively few injuries in the squad.

Rio Ngumoha has become a Liverpool hero at the tender age of 18, but he could have been starring for rivals Manchester United had he chosen the Red Devils over the Merseysiders.

It has been revealed that the English teenage starlet enjoyed a dream Premier League debut in August 2025, coming off the bench to score a 90+10th minute winner in a 3-2 win for Liverpool against Newcastle United. It made him the youngest goalscorer in the club's history.

Recent findings suggest that ngumoha also became only the second 16-year-old to score a winner in the Premier League, following in the footsteps of Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney. Now considered one of the best young players in world football at the age of 18, he could have taken up a similar path to the Red Devils' all-time top goalscorer.

Ngumoha started his youth career as a member of Chelsea's academy but headed to Liverpool in September 2024. The Reds were ordered to reimburse Chelsea a minimum of £2.8 million for Ngumoha's training and development while with the west London outfit.

He was one of the most coveted teenage prospects, with the Merseyside giants seeing off competition from Manchester United to bring him to Anfield.

Industry observers note that the four-cap England international visited United in June 2024 and was informed of what aims the club had for him. They knew that their arch-rivals were in "pole position" to sign him, but they still "pushed for his signature anyway", per The Athletic.

Despite showing Ngumoha around Old Trafford and Carrington, United's efforts were in vain, and he ultimately snubbed them in favour of the Reds.

It has been revealed that the Sun reported that Ngumoha was left "impressed" with the pathway shown by Liverpool, with Conor Bradley and Jarell Quansah (now at Bayer Leverkusen) used as examples. He saw how swiftly they were fast-tracked into the first-team.

According to recent reports, ngumoha started training and playing with the Reds' youth teams but was soon brought into Arne Slot's senior team for first-team training. He has gone from strength to strength ever since. In November 2026, he put in an electric display against United, scoring and recording an assist in his side's resounding 4-0 victory at Anfield.

Ngumoha seemingly turned down the chance to play for the club he supported during his childhood when he opted to join Liverpool last year. He'd revealed in a viral video promoting Adidas F5O boots that he had grown up as a United fan.

It has been revealed that the English wonderkid was asked to choose between club legend David Beckham and current Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham. He responded, "I was a Man United fan, I didn't really watch David Beckham... but I'll have to go David Beckham.".

Ngumoha, born in August 2008, would have been just five when Sir Alex Ferguson retired and oversaw the last campaign in which United won the Premier League title. He wasn't even born when Wayne Rooney and Cristiano Ronaldo lifted the Champions League trophy in Moscow after defeating Chelsea in the final in May 2008.

Industry observers note that man Utd legend Nicky Butt has blasted his former club for not managing to get Ngumoha to put pen-to-paper. He noted on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcas: "He’s a massive Man United fan, and his family – massive Man Utd fan.

“I think he was at 13 or 14 or whatever age it was, he goes and looks around Man United – whether it be Old Trafford or Carrington.

Sources indicate that “He’s gone with his family to look around the football club, and then he’s gone to Liverpool. And he’s picked Liverpool, and he’s a United fan. He should not be allowed out of that building before he signed that contract. It would never have happened.

It has been revealed that “I’d like to know who showed him around the football club. Who’s explaining things? I’d like to think Wayne Rooney or Paul Scholes or Ryan Giggs [were drafted in].”.

The London-born winger isn't the only boyhood Red Devil supporter to play for a rival Premier League club. Cole Palmer was also a fan but has now played for Manchester City and Chelsea.

It’s our duty to promote ourselves: even to other scientists. Am I wrong?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recently, I submitted my faculty file to be considered for promotion.
  • I had an epiphany: if others don’t see the value, that’s on me.
  • Industry observers note that so I withdrew my file and will resubmit it when I have developed a stronger argument for the significance of the fellowship, and will gather support from senior colleagues on its merit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recently, I submitted my faculty file to be considered for promotion. I thought that being elected as a fellow at one of the most prestigious research institutes in my field — bioethics — would strengthen my case. But it seemed that no one I spoke to at my university had heard of the fellowship, and the value of it wasn’t recognized.

I had an epiphany: if others don’t see the value, that’s on me. I need to better communicate why my work matters, rather than assuming that it speaks for itself.

Industry observers note that so I withdrew my file and will resubmit it when I have developed a stronger argument for the significance of the fellowship, and will gather support from senior colleagues on its merit. I know my work is valued outside my own university sphere; now I must make that case internally.

If we want our work to count towards career advancement, it’s up to us to show our peers why it matters.

Am I wrong? — Brandon Brown, public-health and biomedical-ethics specialist at the University of California, Riverside.

“I couldn’t disagree more. I think it’s a shame that scientists need to almost beg their peers to see the value of our work. Most of us invest huge amounts of time, effort and funding into what we do because we genuinely believe it matters. If you truly think your own work is irrelevant unless you can ‘sell it’ to others, then perhaps you’re in the wrong profession.” — Juliana Sanchez Alponti Millar, biologist at the University of York, UK.

“The balancing act of spending your time doing what you think is notable and convincing others about the value is tricky and always there — this is a good example of how you need your colleagues and mentors to understand your motivations and the ‘big plan’.’’ — Russ Altman, bioengineer and geneticist at Stanford University in California.

Industry observers note that “I completely agree with this. As scientists, we often assume our work will speak for itself, but communication and visibility matter a lot. Many of us also lack marketing and self-promotion skills, even though they can make a huge difference in these situations.” — Mariana Belén Galeano, biologist at the University of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

It has been revealed that “The beauty of science is that the scientific process itself sorts out which research is useful. Scientists should do science, publish it and, rather than spend time campaigning for their work, go back and do more science.” — Metin Eren, anthropologist and archaeologist at Kent State University in Kent, Ohio.

“Researchers do need to make their case, but they shouldn’t have to do it alone. Universities must do their part, too: set clear paths to promotion, review progress regularly and make sure managers explain to their staff members how promotion works.” — Timothy Davis, volcanologist at the University of Bristol, UK.

According to recent reports, “We are our own best advocates. It’s taken me some time to shed the modesty and be comfortable with promoting my own work and accolades, but a friend once told me ‘no one cares as much about your career as you do,” and that stuck. You have to show people why they should care.’ — Margaret Swift, ecologist at Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability and Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine in Ithaca, Newly introduced York.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-02203-2.

The 18-year-old grabbed a goal and an assist on his full Premier League debut, becoming the second-youngest to do that in Premier League history after Michael Owen. He also became Spurs' youngest goalscorer in the Premier League, beating Gareth Bale's record.

Supporters have been clamouring for the teen star to be given a run in the team, and his breakthrough performance against Ipswich Town and Saturday may well see them get their wish.

Harry Kane, one of the greatest strikers in Premier League history, was the last player to come through the Tottenham Hotspur academy and become a fully-fledged star and Williams-Barnett could now follow in his footsteps.

And Spurs have rewarded the teenager for his work by offering him a lucrative new contract, which will ward off any potential suitors in the transfer window too.

Williams-Barnett's current deal with Spurs, which he signed last year when turning 17, only runs until 2028, but Tottenham have moved rapidly to extend that, with reports suggesting he is set to put pen-to-paper on that extension in the coming days.

It will be a huge signing for the club, as they look to safeguard the future of one of their biggest stars, but Williams-Barnett is not the only one who is in need of a contract extension at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. There are two other players whose contracts expire in 2028, who are arguably just as important to tie down as the teenager. And they are both players in attacking positions too, which is where Spurs have really struggled under Roberto De Zerbi so far this season.

Spurs have only scored 12 goals in their 11 Premier League games so far in 2026/27, with only three teams in the Premier League table scoring fewer. They have lacked a certain amount of creativity with key players out injured, but a number of them are now slowly getting back in action and working their way back to full fitness.

James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski are key creative outlets for Spurs and both see their current deals expire in north London in 2028.

Sources indicate that kulusevski has hardly played since injuring his knee in May 2025 but is now back as part of the first-team squad. Given his time on the treatment table it may not be a huge pay rise that he gets when he is offered a latest contract, but Spurs have stood by him and there is no doubt that when fully fit he can be a matchwinner, and offering him new terms is imperative.

According to recent reports, maddison on the other hand is a firm fans' favourite, who, like Kulusevski, has had his injury problems. The Englishman is now back playing regularly for the first team, however, and has a huge role to play, not just on the pitch but off it too with his leadership.

Antonio Conte’s recent interview has fuelled speculation of a return to Juventus, but the Bianconeri might have other ideas if Luciano Spalletti leaves.

Conte is undoubtedly part of Juventus’ history, both as a player and as a coach. A serial Serie A champion and a 1996 Champions League winner with the Old Lady, Conte left his mark in Turin also as a coach, winning the first three Scudetti in the post-Calciopoli era.

He returned in 2011 as a coach and left in the summer of 2014 after winning three consecutive Serie A titles.

Sources indicate that his exit still hurts some Juventus supporters, as it materialised one day into the 2014-15 pre-season. Juventus and Conte no longer shared the same view, especially on transfer activity, prompting the Italian tactician to step back and paving the way for Massimiliano Allegri’s appointment.

Conte began Juventus’ remarkable domination of Italian football. Their nine consecutive Serie A titles showcased a winning mentality that often made the difference in their favour among fans using PlayOJO pay by mobile casino UK.

The way it ended, however, upset many Bianconeri supporters, some of whom even started a petition to remove a “star” named after Conte outside the Allianz Stadium after he accepted an offer to become Inter’s coach in 2021.

According to recent reports, over the last 15 years, Conte won Serie A titles with the Nerazzurri and Napoli as well as an FA Cup and a Premier League title with Chelsea. He also coached Tottenham and the Italy national team, remarkably reaching the quarter-finals at the 2016 Euros.

Now, Conte feels the time has come to return to Juventus.

It has been revealed that in his latest interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio, he noted: “I think that sooner or later the circle will close. I know I left something behind, and I know that eventually the circle will close with Juventus.

“There have been moments in the past where we could have reunited, but it’s been difficult because two things have to align. I have to be available, and Juventus have to be looking for a coach who isn’t presently employed.”.

However, as reported by Tuttosport, it remains to be seen whether the Lecce-born coach will fulfil his dream.

Juventus CEO Giovanni Carnevali is not considering sacking Spalletti, who is under contract until 2028, and if Spalletti were to leave at the end of the season, Carnevali would prefer Simone Inzaghi, another ex-Inter coach, over Conte’s return.

Carnevali has often shown his support to Spalletti, including in an interview released in September, after Juventus’ first defeat in 2026-27 against Sassuolo: “Spalletti is an amazing coach, one of the best ever. Changing coaches is not in my nature; we must try to program and build; we must give time and be patient, knowing that we will have to swallow some bitter pills,” remarked the Bianconeri director.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ronald de Boer has revealed just how close he came to joining Manchester United in 2000 before ultimately choosing Rangers following advice from Louis van Gaal.

The former Ajax and Barcelona star held direct talks with Sir Alex Ferguson as he considered leaving Camp Nou, but the competition awaiting him at Old Trafford raised concerns over how regularly he would play.

For De Boer, protecting his place in the Netherlands squad ultimately proved more vital than joining the reigning Premier League champions.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with LiveFootballTickets, De Boer explained that Ferguson was honest about how difficult it would be to guarantee him consistent football.

United already possessed an outstanding midfield containing Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt and David Beckham, with Ferguson planning to rotate heavily.

De Boer was still a Netherlands regular and feared that playing only occasionally at Old Trafford could damage his international prospects.

That led him to seek advice from Van Gaal, who was managing the Netherlands at the time. Van Gaal recommended Rangers, where Dutch coach Dick Advocaat could offer De Boer a more prominent role.

The decision paid off. De Boer spent four years at Ibrox, scoring 40 goals in 129 appearances and helping Rangers win the domestic treble in 2002-03.

From a Man United perspective, it is another fascinating example of the calibre of player Ferguson could attract during the club’s dominant era.

De Boer unquestionably had the technique and experience to succeed at Old Trafford.

However, choosing Rangers made sense.

In an earlier FourFourTwo interview, De Boer also explained that concerns over an existing knee issue and the security of Rangers’ four-year contract influenced his thinking.

Sources indicate that at United, he would have entered arguably the strongest midfield competition in Europe. At Rangers, he became an automatic starter and remained key for his country.

It is easy to imagine what Ferguson might have achieved with another technically gifted Dutch international in his squad, but De Boer’s career suggests he made the right choice for himself.

More than 25 years later, the story also shows that even at United’s peak, guaranteed playing time could still convince elite players to look elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that for Iran, relations with both China and Russia are routinely described as strategic. That relationship looks more complicated from Beijing and Moscow.

Industry observers note that both countries oppose Washington's efforts to isolate Iran and maintain political and economic ties with Tehran. But both have broader interests in their relationships with the United States and may see Iran partly through the prism of their own negotiations with Washington.

That raises a central question: Can Trump's strategy of economically isolating Iran succeed if China and Russia refuse to fully cooperate?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

China is currently the most important destination for Iranian oil.

In 2025, it was reported that Chinese buyers took more than 80% of Iran's seaborne crude exports, much of it through independent refiners and at a steep discount because of sanctions.

As China provided Tehran an economic lifeline, Iran also became increasingly dependent on Chinese manufactured goods, machinery and industrial inputs.

Mohsen Solhdoost, an assistant professor of international relations at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, says China is key to Washington's strategy but not decisive on its own.

"If the objective is to reduce Iranian export earnings, restrict access to equipment and make economic and military recovery more difficult, the United States can achieve substantial results without Chinese cooperation," he told DW.

But forcing Iran to accept Washington's preferred nuclear or regional policies is another matter.

"The ability to interrupt trade is much easier to demonstrate than the ability to determine another government's political choices," Solhdoost mentioned.

That distinction has become more important as US sanctions enforcement and maritime blockade efforts have increased pressure on Iranian crude oil exports.

In November, Washington announced Task Force Iron Gate, an initiative aimed at disrupting the movement of sanctioned goods, military equipment and revenue through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

It has been revealed that even so, these trade links have not disappeared. The commercial and security interests of countries including Iraq, Pakistan and Turkey mean that goods continue to move across the region, albeit under greater scrutiny.

Industry observers note that as a result, China's role in Iran's economy remains significant, but Solhdoost argues that demand alone cannot sustain Iranian exports. The oil must be able to reach international markets.

"A Chinese buyer cannot keep Iranian export revenues flowing simply by remaining willing to buy if newly loaded tankers cannot reach the market," Solhdoost stated.

This economic pressure is shaping Tehran's financial planning. A senior official at Iran's Plan and Budget Organization recently said the government was preparing its 2027-2028 budget under several scenarios, including one in which oil revenue falls to zero.

That does not mean Iran has adopted a zero-oil budget, but considering such a scenario illustrates how seriously Tehran views the situation. At the same time, Chinese trade can preserve critical parts of the Iranian economy even if overall commerce shrinks.

Machinery, electronics, spare parts and industrial components can still reach Iran by rail and road. Such trade cannot replace maritime commerce at comparable scale or cost, but it can keep selected factories and infrastructure operating.

Such Chinese support could help Iran endure pressure without preventing economic deterioration, states Solhdoost.

But even for Beijing, supporting Iran economically does not mean supporting every Iranian policy.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has maintained support for cooperation with Tehran while calling for negotiations, safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and stable energy supplies.

According to recent reports, A prolonged conflict around Hormuz threatens wider energy supplies and global shipping. China therefore benefits from continued access to Iranian oil but also from regional stability.

Russia creates another obstacle to Iran's isolation. The two countries share access to the Caspian Sea and have expanded military, transport and economic cooperation.

Iranian officials have discussed ways of using Russian and northern trade routes to reduce the impact of American restrictions. There has also been speculation about oil swaps and deeper Russian assistance, although these claims remain difficult to verify.

Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East, believes the summit should be viewed within a larger attempt to manage the wars in both Ukraine and the Middle East.

"Russia, China and the United States appear to be seeking constructive dialogue and results that could shape a upcoming security architecture in the international system," Vakhshiteh told DW.

Solhdoost also warns against overstating Russian support for Iran.

The strategic partnership between Moscow and Tehran provides for security cooperation and efforts to counter unilateral sanctions, but it does not require Russia to enter a war on Iran's behalf.

Since Russia is deeply engaged in Ukraine, it likely has its own priorities in negotiations with Washington, indicates Solhdoost.

"Russia would prioritize its own national interests in negotiations with the US over Ukraine and Iran," he said.

Moscow could support Iran while simultaneously using its relationship with Tehran as leverage in talks with Trump over Ukraine.

For Iran, ties with China and Russia remain essential. They provide alternative trade routes, export markets and diplomatic support that complicate Washington's efforts to isolate Tehran.

Yet neither Beijing nor Moscow views Iran solely through the lens of strategic partnership. Both weigh support for Tehran against their own economic interests, security concerns and dealings with Washington.

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026.

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer.

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season.

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

According to recent reports, ‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

Recent findings suggest that ‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’.

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

In a recent development, ‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts says. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the plans as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

Sources indicate that ‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’.

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Recent findings suggest that potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

In Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

Sources indicate that ‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he says. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’.

According to recent reports, he is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

Industry observers note that ‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he claims. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a latest language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'.

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe.

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday.

According to recent reports, potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his latest surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

It has been revealed that he has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'.

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season.

Sources indicate that attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

Sources indicate that ‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’.

A longer version, which includes a pointed dig at neighbours Birmingham City, survives in Villa folklore, but isn't often sung on matchdays now.

According to recent reports, the captain's chant is regularly one of the loudest at Villa Park, as fans came up with it soon after McGinn arrived from Hibernian in 2018. The lyrics have been updated from season to season as the dugout has changed, from Steve Bruce to Dean Smith, Steven Gerrard and now Emery. Esposito certainly fits the profile Arsenal should be targeting.

Industry observers note that at 21, he already possesses the physical presence of a traditional No.9 while showing impressive movement, finishing and link-up play. He could eventually give Arteta a long-term focal point rather than another short-term solution.

The problem is Inter’s negotiating position.

In a recent development, A €60m offer has already failed, and with a contract running until 2032 there is absolutely no pressure to sell. Arsenal would probably need to go considerably higher simply to start serious discussions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul stated Thursday's meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" in Berlin sent a strong signal to Moscow that it was time to take negotiations to end the war in Ukraine seriously.

It has been revealed that speaking to DW during a visit to the South Caucasus, Wadephul described the summit as the largest meeting of Ukraine's supporters so far. The meeting represents the 18th set of high-level talks among the coalition's members.

He said it demonstrated that allies remained firmly behind Kyiv in the fifth year of Russia's war and were ready to do "what was necessary to ensure Ukraine could negotiate from a position of strength.".

"The summit itself is already a success," he told DW.

Sources indicate that wadephul also welcomed the US initiative to restart peace negotiations. After nine months without progress, an initial meeting had taken place in Abu Dhabi, with a follow-up round planned and European participation expected.

"We are also preparing for the possibility that the negotiations will not be successful and that, over the coming winter, we will have to continue supplying Ukraine with heating, electricity and all essential supplies, including water," he said.

"And we will continue to stand by Ukraine militarily.".

He stressed that any peace agreement must include security guarantees to protect Ukraine against future Russian attacks.

In earlier comments during his trip to the South Caucasus, Wadephul said that Ukraine and Europe must be involved in any negotiations over the future of Ukraine.

Wadephul did, however, welcome the trilateral meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

"Every conversation that takes place is a good conversation," he told DW during a visit to Azerbaijan on Wednesday.

Later on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin mentioned he had invited Europeans to Moscow for talks on the potential structure of future talks to end the war.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Download the Nature Podcast 23 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that late last week the UN’s climate conference, COP31, failed to reach a consensus on its headline message. That news came on the heels of the UN acknowledging that the 1.5 ˚C warming limit set out in Paris will be breached. So, it’s easy to feel anxious in a world where it seems that not enough is being done about climate change. But is it possible to overcome such anxiety or even use it?

In the final episode of Cooked? I open up about my own climate anxiety and discover that there are still things that I can do to battle climate change. And how those small individual actions could potentially lead to more systemic change.

00:00 Can I do anything about my climate anxiety?

04:43 What the science states about ‘ecoanxiety’.

11:35 Can individuals really do anything?

18:44 How we can create bigger change.

Net zero emissions won’t reverse climate change — some nations look to ‘net negative’.

The rise of eco-anxiety: scientists wake up to the mental-health toll of climate change.

According to recent reports, nick Petrić Howe: As I said, I’ve struggled with anxiety about climate change. Sometimes I feel paralysed by how hopeless it all seems. Nicolo Barella insists that it is not all doom and gloom for Inter after the disappointing end to their Serie A match away against Atalanta over the weekend, and while they will have an opportunity to redeem themselves in the Champions League on Wednesday night, the Italy international says that his biggest goal is to cement back-to-back Serie A titles.

Barella spoke to the media alongside Cristian Chivu at a press conference on Tuesday, ahead of Inter’s Champions League league phase clash against VfB Stuttgart on Wednesday evening.

Inter have won two and lost two of their first four games in the competition this season and will face a Stuttgart side that start the week one point and one position better off than the Nerazzurri in the table.

It has been revealed that barella was asked several questions about Inter’s 4-4 draw against Atalanta on Sunday night. The Nerazzurri had led 3-1 for well over an hour, but a particularly poor final 10 minutes saw them come away with just one point.

Barella was asked by reporters on Tuesday whether he thinks Inter need to make a leap forward in quality as a team.

It has been revealed that “Yes,” he agreed. “I’ve always noted that the team makes the difference. I’ve always been around strong players ever since I joined Inter. I think it’s a great dressing room. Sometimes we could handle certain situations better. It’s a responsibility that is on us, we have discussed it among ourselves.

Recent findings suggest that “If I had the solution in front of me, it would all be very easy, but we have to continue working to improve the situation. It’s part of football.”.

Barella shrugged off suggestions that Inter do not have the right mentality.

In a recent development, “There are great players in the dressing room. We play with 11 and the subs aren’t a problem either. Everyone who comes on always adds something.

“We took the lead in Bergamo, and once they’d caught up with us, it was everybody’s responsibility. Maybe our attention dropped. We couldn’t afford to come home from Bergamo with just a point. It’s easy to say it now, but it’s clear that there will be slip-ups over the course of a season. I see the glass as being half full.”.

Asked how Inter will cope with the absences of Hakan Calhanoglu and Piotr Zielinski against Stuttgart, Barella said: “All absences weigh heavily because we have so many matches. Having lots of different solutions is an advantage. We will miss them.

According to recent reports, “We have to play as the best version of ourselves. We’ve seen Stuttgart’s characteristics. We will give everything we have and we want to do so.”.

It has been revealed that asked for a word on Pio Esposito, whose hat-trick against Atalanta was not enough to secure the three points, Barella said: “Pio’s maturity was shown in his post-match interview as well. He said he didn’t want to score three goals if they weren’t going to count for anything.

“It’s true that when you hit rock bottom, you try to give yourself a bit of a push, but over the last few years, Inter’s first thought has always been to go out and fight on all fronts. Some years we did better than others. I don’t think it’s a matter of failure, but that there will be ups and downs. It’s a team game and it is possible that sometimes Inter drops off.”.

Barella insisted that Inter can’t afford to give preference to one competition over another, but admitted that he does want to go back-to-back as Serie A champions by the end of the season.

Industry observers note that “We can’t think like that. I think the last team to win two consecutive league titles was Juve, and our goal is to confirm ourselves as champions. That’s our stimulus, and obviously we also have the Champions League and other competitions to respect.”.

In a recent development, atlético Madrid has completed the purchase of half of Atlético Fútbol Club, the Guayaquil side that won Ecuador's Serie B in its first season. The deal gives the Spanish club its first affiliate in South America before the Ecuadorian team steps up to Serie A in 2027.

The announcement went up on the Madrid club’s website at 19:00 on 13 November 2026.

Sources indicate that the move had been signalled earlier in the year. On Friday 20 February 2026, Atlético said it would share sporting, institutional and commercial expertise with Atlético FC and might take a stake in the following months, El Comercio reported.

Regarded as Ecuador’s largest non-profit organisation, the Junta de Beneficencia de Guayaquil operates in all 24 of the country’s provinces.

The club’s route into Serie B was unusual. It took over the place of Atlético Vinotinto, which could not use it because its affiliate Vinotinto FC had been relegated. The team also changed its name from Atlético JBG to Atlético FC.

Promotion came on 15 October 2026 with a 1-0 win over Independiente Juniors. Fidel Martínez scored the goal. A week later, on Thursday 22 October, a 2-2 draw against Cuenca Juniors at the Estadio Alejandro Serrano sealed the title. That match was the ninth round of the promotion hexagonal.

Industry observers note that across the campaign the side scored 39 goals and conceded 21. It became the 37th different club to win Ecuador’s Serie B. The team is coached by Carlos Santamarina, who comes from Atlético’s academy.

Recent findings suggest that the promotion also reshapes the city’s football map. Guayaquil will have four clubs in the 2027 Serie A: Atlético FC, Barcelona SC, Emelec and Guayaquil City.

Mexico and Canada already host clubs in the Madrid side’s network of linked teams, through Atlético de San Luis and Atlético Ottawa.

The investment builds on years of groundwork in Ecuador. Atlético and the Junta signed their original strategic agreement on Monday 24 July 2023 at the charity’s sports complex. Under that deal, the club’s academy would apply its coaching model to the Junta’s football division. At the time, that division served 2,500 children from vulnerable backgrounds.

It has been revealed that in June 2026 the club put the number of young players at more than 14,000. That same month, chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín visited the academy’s Guayaquil base. With the Junta’s delegation, he watched an Atlético FC match and greeted Santamarina.

Industry observers note that for recent followers of Manchester City, the club is synonymous with hoisting trophies and having deep pockets. However, it's crucial to remember the bad times that paved the way to the club's recent glory. Except for the Golden Era in the late 1960s, City's faithful endured decades of playing second fiddle to their neighbours in red. Winters of defeat followed by more defeat. But through the heartaches and let-downs, the fans would unite at Maine Road, belting out their anthems every Saturday.

Now, a fresh chapter under Enzo Maresca is adding fresh verses to the Citizens' songbook.

From the timeless "Blue Moon" to the spirited "City 'til I Die," we invite you to dive into the electric atmosphere in the stands and discover how these chants have become an indelible part of Manchester City's story.

"Blue moon, you saw me standing alone,.

Sources indicate that "Blue Moon" is the most iconic Manchester City chant. It's a classic song that reflects the club's heritage. The "Blue Moon" refers to City's blue colors, and the lyrics are a declaration of love and support for the team. The tune originates from the American songwriting duo of composer Richard Rodgers and lyricist Lorenz Hart and never fails to get the supporters massively revved up.

It's not as old a City tradition as many assume. The song was first sung by Crewe Alexandra fans, and club historian Gary James traces City's adoption to the opening game of the 1989/90 season at Liverpool, where a handful of fans started singing it on the way out of Anfield.

Just like the fans of the Invisible Man,.

According to recent reports, this chant is a nod to the die-hard City fans who are always there to support the team, no matter where they play. The reference to the "Invisible Man" playfully suggests that City fans are everywhere.

Its origins are disputed. The most popular story is that it was born at a Millwall away game City fans had been banned from attending. These days it is a ready-made reply whenever rivals taunt City for having no fans.

We're the famous Manchester City,.

This chant celebrates Manchester City being top of the pile and highlights their accomplishments, including winning league titles and cups. The fans no doubt take great pleasure in singing this one having spent so much time at the bottom in previous eras.

Sources indicate that its roots go back further than most realise. Known originally as the 'Viking Call', it was first performed by City fans on 23 October 1976 against Ipswich. For years it was little more than a drawn-out "City" chant with the rest of the tune hummed, and the 'best team in the land' words were only added later.

Action Images via Reuters/Jason Cairnduff.

It has been revealed that this chant is a simple yet powerful declaration of lifelong loyalty to Manchester City. It signifies that fans are devoted to the club until the end of their lives.

This chant is in honour of former Manchester City striker Shaun Goater, who was known as "The Goat." A classic example of the dry wit of the long-suffering football fans, this song celebrated a man who may not have been the most talented but was dearly beloved and an important talisman during a difficult era.

Set to the tune of 'Hey Jude' by the Beatles, this is a staple vibe around the Etihad Stadium, often adding to the lively atmosphere among the fans and sure to be roared around the stadium during the big clashes.

A modern era set to the tune of the 90s banger - 'Rhythm is a dancer.' The City massive can be seen at Brighton away getting amongst it to this chant at Brighton away.

Oh when the Blues go marching in,.

Oh when the Blues go marching in.".

This chant is a variation of the classic "When the Saints Go Marching In." It's a lively and rhythmic chant expressing the desire to be part of the City's triumphs.

In a recent development, the "Poznan" chant involves fans turning their backs to the pitch and linking arms, swaying from side to side, reminiscent of the famous celebration performed by fans of Polish club Lech Poznań. It's a fun and visually striking chant and one that the City fans have become known for.

It has been revealed that city supporters first saw it when Lech's fans performed it at the Etihad in a Europa League group game on 21 October 2010, and they adopted it soon after. It enjoyed a revival in 2025 when Oasis encouraged crowds to do the Poznan on their reunion tour, which prompted Lech to send Noel Gallagher a thank-you letter and a personalised shirt.

LaLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

In a recent development, javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

According to recent reports, the list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas indicates Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

Industry observers note that earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez remarked Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

It has been revealed that tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

The thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club said Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

It has been revealed that the same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas mentioned the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

The dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid mentioned it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

Their representatives will gather at Ciudad Real Madrid’s basketball venue for two assemblies called by the board, with remote attendance also possible. Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee is reportedly being eyed by Como after the Serie A side were dealt a devastating injury blow to Moise Kean.

The Dutchman has made 11 appearances for the Red Devils so far this season but every one of those has come as a substitute, with his 45 minutes off the bench at Anfield on Sunday the longest runout he’s had in the current campaign (Transfermarkt).

He turned down the opportunity to join Fiorentina during the summer transfer window, but rumours over a potential return to Italy for the ex-Bologna marksman refuse to go away.

According to Gianluca di Marzio, Como are interested in Zirkzee as a potential centre-forward acquisition for the January transfer window as they seek attacking reinforcements after Kean aggravated an existing injury, thus ruling out for an extended period.

The report adds that the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick’s successor is ‘another variable to consider’ as to whether the new boss will green-light an exit for the Nerherlands forward.

Even with Benjamin Sesko sidelined, Zirkzee has struggled to get much of a look-in for United so far this season, but perhaps Pochettino might be more willing to give him a fair crack than Carrick had been.

Despite him playing just 231 minutes in the current campaign, only three teammates have scored more than the Dutchman’s two goals, and he has the best goals-per-minute ratio of anyone to have found the net for the Red Devils in 2026/27 (Transfermarkt).

One of those strikes came in the form of a stoppage-time consolation against Como last month, with that 4-1 victory for Cesc Fabregas’ side helping the Champions League debutants to the lofty heights of fourth in the table at the midway point of the league phase.

Gaz Drinkwater of BBC Radio Manchester‘s The Devils’ Advocate podcast described the 25-year-old as ‘slick’ on the ball, but also lacking the pace required to succeed in the Premier League, with a record of only six goals in 63 English top-flight games.

How much game-time Zirkzee is handed between now and the end of December will tell a lot as to how highly Pochettino regards him. The latest dugout change at Old Trafford might afford the number 11 a upcoming lease of life; conversely, it could push him towards the exit door if he continues to be left feeding off scraps.

Once again, the 25-year-old’s future is set to be a pertinent talking point in the run-up to a transfer window.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luis Enrique has warned Paris Saint-Germain that Roma will cause them problems in the Champions League on Wednesday, and praised Gian Piero Gasperini for building teams with a “very clear playing identity”.

With quotes via PSG’s official website, the Spaniard was speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Wednesday’s league-phase clash at the Parc des Princes. Kick-off is at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT].

Industry observers note that the two sides are heading in very different directions in Europe. PSG sit top of the league phase with a perfect record of 12 points from four matches, having scored 20 goals and conceded just five, while Roma are 20th with four points.

“It’s clear we’re happy to be back in the Champions League, and above all at home,” Luis Enrique said. “This match will be very different from what we’ve experienced so far. They’re a team that defends in a particular way, but we can’t wait.

According to recent reports, “They’re a team that loses very few matches. We know it will be very difficult, and it’ll be a great challenge. If we win this game, it’ll be the first time we’ve won five matches in a row in the league phase, so that would be a first!”.

Sources indicate that luis Enrique had plenty of praise for Gasperini. The two crossed paths in 2011, when the Spaniard was in charge at Roma and Gasperini lasted only a few weeks at Inter.

Industry observers note that “He’s a coach with a lot of experience, and I like him a lot. His teams have a very clear playing identity, very different from what we’re used to coming up against,” he said.

It has been revealed that “I remember he was at Inter when I was coaching Roma. It was complicated for him there, but he proved afterwards what he was capable of. We know they’ll cause us problems tomorrow, and it’s a great challenge.”.

It has been revealed that the holders will be without two of their biggest names. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during PSG’s win over Barcelona last month, and Désiré Doué also faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a suspected ACL injury.

According to recent reports, “That’s football at the highest level. Every team and every coach goes through it. There are injuries,” Luis Enrique said. “It’s very sad to have this type of injury for players like Désiré and Kvara, but we’re focusing on their recovery and how we can improve our performance.

“This team has shown all its resilience over the last three years. We’ve always bounced back from everything.”.

He also ruled out signing a short-term replacement in January.

“We don’t have to sign anyone in the transfer window, and it’s not our style to sign a player for six months. We’re happy with our squad. Above all, we’re not afraid of anything. We’re confident in our ability and our resilience.”.

The former Roma coach was also asked about his time in the Italian capital.

“My time at Roma was very special for me, and I have great memories. It’s a magnificent city, I experienced some lovely things there as a coach, and I’m at peace with everything that happened to me there.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Zverev misrepresented the result of his 2024 domestic abuse trial, causing harm to his former partner and the mother of his child, Brenda Patea's lawyer has told DW.

The case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement. Zverev, who won the French and US Open in 2026, is alleged to have told French publication L'Equipe that: "I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.".

Industry observers note that as Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued... without any finding of guilt, and the presumption of innocence remains unaffected.".

However, Zverev's statement has harmed Patea's standing and her career as an influencer, according to her lawyer, Michael Scheele.

Industry observers note that "What she suffered after this interview in L'Equipe was published is nothing but a shitstorm. It's also detrimental to her business," Scheele told DW.

"We still don't know the truth objectively and we have an agreement in which he committed not to talk about the incident and the case at all," he added.

According to recent reports, however, in the statement sent to DW, Zverev's lawyers asserted that "there has been no breach of any contractual obligations or violation of Ms. Patea’s personality rights.".

Zverev had made similar comments before. On the day the settlement was reached, the tennis pro spoke to reporters at the 2024 French Open.

According to recent reports, "That's what dropping the case is: That is innocence. They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day," he stated.

The lawsuit, seen by DW, states that Zverev should be subject to "a fine of up to €250,000 ($275,000) to be determined for each instance of violation — and, in the event that such fine cannot be collected, substitute custodial detention of up to six months," should he be found guilty.

Zverev's lawyers reject the allegations.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit. If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion protected by Article 5(1) of the German Basic Law," they noted.

It has been revealed that "Our client would merely have expressed his personal conviction that he had done everything in his power to refute the allegations made against him and that he considers his innocence to have been confirmed by the outcome of the criminal proceedings. "He is fully entitled to hold and express this view.".

The law firm, Schertz Bergmann, added that: "Unlike the opposing counsel, we intend to conduct these proceedings in court rather than in the press.".

Scheele said he and his client did not want to go back to court but were frustrated in their efforts to resolve matters in other ways.

According to recent reports, "We went forward writing to him in a polite way, asking him to sign and to declare that he's not going to repeat what he stated. And he didn't reply. So we wrote twice more, no reply.

It has been revealed that "That's when we had to decide to go to court, which was not the aim at the beginning. We wanted to avoid it, but we had no other choice.".

Zverev, now resident in Monaco, is at the moment playing in the season-ending ATP Finals tournament in Turin.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A court in Asturias has convicted the Real Oviedo supporter who made monkey gestures at Kylian Mbappé of a hate crime.
  • The Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime.
  • The abuse came during Real Oviedo v Real Madrid on 24 August 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A court in Asturias has convicted the Real Oviedo supporter who made monkey gestures at Kylian Mbappé of a hate crime. The case adds to a growing list of criminal convictions for racist abuse of Real Madrid players in Spanish grounds.

The Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime. The Second Section of the Audiencia Provincial de Asturias delivered the verdict on 17 November 2026. It was a verdict by agreement, known in Spain as conformidad.

The abuse came during Real Oviedo v Real Madrid on 24 August 2025. The fan made monkey gestures and noises in the 37th minute. Real Madrid’s players were celebrating Mbappé’s opening goal at the time.

Industry observers note that the man will not go to prison as long as he keeps to the terms of his sentence. The term is suspended on condition that he stays away from football stadiums hosting official competitions for two years, Real Madrid said in an official statement. The prosecuting parties also tied the suspension to a ban from LaLiga stadiums and a ban on approaching Mbappé. The defendant accepted these conditions.

According to recent reports, the fine was set at six months at a daily rate of €8. He is also barred from working in education, teaching, sport or leisure for three years and 11 months.

The case was charged under article 510.2.a of the Spanish Criminal Code. LaLiga filed the original complaint. It also supplied expert lip-reading evidence that proved key to resolving the case. Real Madrid later joined the proceedings as a private prosecutor.

The ruling is LaLiga’s twelfth conviction for racism in Spanish football, Servimedia reported. The league presented the outcome as proof of its commitment to fighting racism.

Industry observers note that the Carlos Tartiere has featured in this list before. In April 2026, a supporter was convicted over abuse of Marcus Rashford at Real Oviedo v FC Barcelona. That person received a nine-month prison sentence. Another conviction, handed down in September 2025, followed abuse of Iñaki Williams at an Espanyol v Athletic Club match from the 2019/20 season.

According to recent reports, for Real Madrid, the verdict extends a run of cases involving its own players. The club has listed earlier convictions for racist abuse at Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and the José Zorrilla. The Valladolid case ended on 21 May 2025. The Audiencia Provincial de Valladolid convicted five people of hate crimes for abusing Vinícius Júnior at the José Zorrilla on 30 December 2022. Each received a one-year prison sentence.

Real Madrid is now acting as private prosecutor in other cases involving similar incidents against its players.
